verses.text: When Abram was ninety-nine years old, the LORD appeared to him and said, "I am God Almighty. Walk before Me and be blameless.
I will establish My covenant between Me and you, and I will multiply you exceedingly."
Then Abram fell facedown, and God said to him,
"As for Me, this is My covenant with you: You will be the father of many nations.
No longer will you be called Abram, but your name will be Abraham, for I have made you a father of many nations.
I will make you exceedingly fruitful; I will make nations of you, and kings will descend from you.
I will establish My covenant as an everlasting covenant between Me and you and your descendants after you, to be your God and the God of your descendants after you.
And to you and your descendants I will give the land where you are residing—all the land of Canaan—as an eternal possession; and I will be their God."
God also said to Abraham, "You must keep My covenant—you and your descendants in the generations after you.
This is My covenant with you and your descendants after you, which you are to keep: Every male among you must be circumcised.
You are to circumcise the flesh of your foreskin, and this will be a sign of the covenant between Me and you.

Generation after generation, every male must be circumcised when he is eight days old, including those born in your household and those purchased from a foreigner—even those who are not your offspring.
Whether they are born in your household or purchased, they must be circumcised. My covenant in your flesh will be an everlasting covenant.
But if any male is not circumcised, he will be cut off from his people; he has broken My covenant."
Then God said to Abraham, "As for Sarai your wife, do not call her Sarai, for her name is to be Sarah.
And I will bless her and will surely give you a son by her. I will bless her, and she will be the mother of nations; kings of peoples will descend from her."
Abraham fell facedown. Then he laughed and said to himself, "Can a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old? Can Sarah give birth at the age of ninety?"
And Abraham said to God, "O that Ishmael might live under Your blessing!"
But God replied, "Your wife Sarah will indeed bear you a son, and you are to name him Isaac. I will establish My covenant with him as an everlasting covenant for his descendants after him.
As for Ishmael, I have heard you, and I will surely bless him; I will make him fruitful and multiply him greatly. He will become the father of twelve rulers, and I will make him into a great nation.
But I will establish My covenant with Isaac, whom Sarah will bear to you at this time next year."
When He had finished speaking with Abraham, God went up from him.

On that very day Abraham took his son Ishmael and all those born in his household or purchased with his money—every male among the members of Abraham's household—and he circumcised them, just as God had told him.
So Abraham was ninety-nine years old when he was circumcised,
and his son Ishmael was thirteen;
Abraham and his son Ishmael were circumcised on the same day.
And all the men of Abraham's household—both servants born in his household and those purchased from foreigners—were circumcised with him.

context.author: Genesis names no author. Jewish and Christian tradition, and the New Testament’s way of speaking of “the Law of Moses” (Luke 24:44), credit the five books of the Law to Moses. Many scholars think Genesis was gathered and shaped from older sources over a long time, and a few remarks look back from a later day: “at that time the Canaanites were in the land” (Genesis 12:6).
context.genre: Family narrative: the story of Abraham, Sarah and their family (Genesis 11:27 to 25:11)
context.audience: Israel, the children of Abraham, learning how God’s promise began
context.setting: When Abram is ninety-nine, the LORD appears: “I am God Almighty. Walk before Me and be blameless” (v.1). Abram falls facedown (v.3). God makes him “the father of many nations” and changes his name: “No longer will you be called Abram, but your name will be Abraham” (vv.4-5). Kings will come from him, the covenant will be everlasting, and all the land of Canaan will belong to his descendants (vv.6-8). The sign of the covenant is circumcision: “Every male among you must be circumcised,” at eight days old, including servants (vv.10-14). Sarai’s name becomes Sarah, and she will be “the mother of nations” (vv.15-16). Abraham falls facedown again and laughs: “Can a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old?” (v.17). He asks that Ishmael might live under God’s blessing; God will bless Ishmael and make him a great nation, but His covenant will be with Isaac, whom Sarah will bear next year (vv.18-21). That same day Abraham, Ishmael and every male of the household are circumcised (vv.23-27).
context.custom: Circumcision was practiced by Egyptians and other peoples, often at puberty or before marriage. In Israel it was done on the eighth day, to an infant who could do nothing but receive it, and it marked the whole family as belonging to the covenant. A new name meant a new identity given by a superior: Pharaoh renamed Joseph (41:45) and Nebuchadnezzar renamed Daniel (Daniel 1:7). Abram means ‘exalted father’; Abraham sounds like ‘father of a multitude.’
context.timelineImmediate: Chapter 18 tells how the LORD visited Abraham at Mamre, promised a son within a year, and heard Abraham plead for Sodom.
context.timelineBible: Paul says Abraham “received the sign of circumcision as a seal of the righteousness that he had by faith while he was still uncircumcised” (Romans 4:11). Moses and the prophets call for circumcision of the heart (Deuteronomy 10:16; Jeremiah 4:4), and Paul says, “circumcision is a matter of the heart, by the Spirit” (Romans 2:29). Colossians links it to baptism (Colossians 2:11-12). Jesus was circumcised on the eighth day and named (Luke 2:21).

translation.meaning: El Shaddai, ‘God Almighty.’ Its root meaning is debated: ‘the mountain one,’ or ‘the one who is sufficient.’ The patriarchs know God by this name (Exodus 6:3).
Whole, complete, without blemish. Used of sacrificial animals with no defect, and of Noah (6:9).
To circumcise, cut off. The sign of the covenant cut in the body.

gospelParallels.note: Abraham received circumcision as a seal of the righteousness of faith.
Circumcision is a matter of the heart, by the Spirit.
Circumcised with a circumcision not done by hands.

otBackground.note: I appeared to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob as God Almighty.
On the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin is to be circumcised.

overview.summary: God Almighty renews His covenant with Abram, names him Abraham, father of many nations, and Sarai Sarah, gives circumcision as the covenant’s sign, and promises that Sarah will bear Isaac within a year.
overview.settingLine: Abraham’s household, thirteen years after Ishmael.

history.t: Known in Egypt, but here on the eighth day.
A greater one gives a new identity.

customs.t: Servants are included in the covenant.

archaeology.t: A tomb relief at Saqqara (about 2350 BC) shows a circumcision.
The Greek historian (5th century BC) wrote that Egyptians practiced circumcision.

overview.discussion: Abraham laughed at God’s promise (v.17), and God still named the child Isaac, ‘he laughs.’ What promise of God seems laughable to me right now?
overview.book: The book of Genesis · 50 chapters (1-25 in the app so far). Beginnings: creation, the fall, the flood and the nations, then God’s promise to Abraham and his family.
overview.author: Moses, by tradition
